items.question: How are images resized without uploading to a server?
items.answer: Images are decoded directly into browser memory using modern HTML5 Canvas and `createImageBitmap` APIs with high-quality bicubic resampling. The resized image is generated as a Blob in your browser, completely avoiding network uploads.

items.question: How is the aspect ratio maintained when resizing?
items.answer: When the ratio lock is active, changing width automatically computes height: `newH = max(1, round(newW × origH / origW))`. Conversely, altering height recalculates width proportionally.

items.question: What image formats can I resize and export?
items.answer: The resizer accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP formats. You can export the output image as JPEG, PNG, or modern compressed WebP.

items.question: Does resizing also reduce image file size?
items.answer: Yes. Downscaling image resolution significantly reduces pixel count and uncompressed byte size. You can also fine-tune output JPEG/WebP quality to achieve optimal file size reduction.

items.question: What happens to transparency when converting PNG to JPEG?
items.answer: JPEG does not support alpha transparency channels. When exporting transparent images to JPEG, the canvas automatically fills transparent regions with clean solid white.

items.question: What are the maximum resolution limits?
items.answer: Most desktop browsers easily handle photos up to 50 megapixels. For mobile devices, browser canvas dimensions are safely managed to prevent memory crashes.

items.question: Does the resizer preserve correct camera orientation?
items.answer: Yes. We decode images with `{ imageOrientation: "from-image" }`, ensuring EXIF orientation metadata is automatically respected so your portrait or rotated photos display upright.

items.question: Are my personal images uploaded or logged?
items.answer: No. Zero bytes of your photos leave your computer. Processing occurs entirely in client-side RAM and memory is freed immediately upon download or reset.
